newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian forward dollar premia dips on CRR reports.
newsitem.headline: Indian forward dollar premia dips on CRR reports.

text.p: Indian premia on forward dollar transactions opened sharply lower on Thursday as newspapers continued to report on an impending cut in cash reserve ratio (CRR) for banks, bank dealers said.
Premia for April dollars opened at 1.66/1.69 rupees on Thursday, down from the previous close of 1.79/1.82 rupees, dealers said. Premia on shorter-term dollars also fell.
Last week, newspapers said a 0.5-1.0 percent cut in CRR is being planned by the central bank in its credit policy to be released later this month.
The Business Standard on Thursday said the industry ministry, "alarmed by trends pointing to an industrial slowdown," urged the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to effect a 3.0-5.0 percent cut in CRR.
"There is general receiving interest because of expectations of interest rates coming down," said a bank dealer.
"Exporters are also looking at selling their dollars at the premia levels available now," he said.
He said six month premium has bottomed out at around 8.0 percent annualised. "It shouldn't fall below even when the CRR cuts happens," he said.
Most dealers said the RBI is unlikely to cut CRR by more than two percent. Currently CRR is 12 percent.
Inter-bank call rates were seen edging down after opening at 10.65/10.90 percent on Thursday.

"The comfortable liquidity position in the month of October and expectations of a reserve cut in the credit policy should see call rates ease to single digit levels," said ICICI Securities and Finance Company in a debt market update.
